The system is a well-built local coordination tool for Claude Code + Hermes, backed by `router.py`, a CLI (`cli.py`), and a web app (`app/server.py`), with solid existing test coverage. I found five concrete, codebase-grounded gaps rather than cosmetic nitpicks — writing these up as a plan document now.

> Write agent_router/IMPROVEMENTS.md
Now writing the handoff note for Hermes to review.

> Write agent_state/handoff.md
I planned 5 improvements for the agent_router system (not Applio proper — this task was scoped to the router itself) and wrote them to `agent_router/IMPROVEMENTS.md`:

1. **Non-atomic tasks.md writes** — readers don't take the lock that writers do, risking a truncated table under concurrent CLI/app/router access.
2. **No stale-run recovery** — a crashed router leaves `in_progress` tasks stuck, requiring manual tasks.md edits.
3. **Relay mode never resumes sessions between turns** — unlike the reply path, so every relay turn re-sends full context cold.
4. **No aggregated cost visibility** — per-turn cost is parsed but discarded, despite relay's up-to-4x turn multiplier.
5. **Unbounded in-memory output buffering** during a run, only truncated after the fact.

No code was changed — this was a planning task. Handoff is written for Hermes to review the plan in `agent_state/handoff.md`.
